app: Retina/DPR image-token two-tier replication (mirror of macOS finding)
channel_setup: Same duel page captured at DPR=1 and DPR=2; src/image-tokens.mjs (API downscale tiers) vs structured view.

t1_read_text.detail: DPR=1 (1280x800): 1366 img tok both tiers vs 438 structured (3.12x). DPR=2 (2560x1600): high-res tier 4784 tok (10.92x), legacy tier 1534 tok (3.50x) — EXACT replication of the macOS numbers on Linux via DPR emulation. Confirms the pixel cost of a screen is set by an API-side downscale rule, not by the harness.

measurements.notes: Structured cost is DPR-invariant (438 tok at both DPRs); pixel cost is not. High-DPI is where the structured channel's advantage is largest on high-res models (10.9x) and where a legacy-tier model silently discards the resolution paid for.

runtime_verification.method: PNG header dims read back; helper formulas vs macOS cell
